HostAuth.description: How to authenticate pack downloads from one host.

env.description: Environment variable holding the token, e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

header.description: Header that carries the token; default `Authorization`.

scheme.description: Text before the token, default `Bearer`; empty sends the token alone.

SigningConfig.description: Which pack signatures to trust; official packs ship inside cuilo and need none.

keys.description: Trusted minisign public keys by name, e.g. `acme = "RWQ…"`.

require.description: Refuse packs without a valid signature from a trusted key.

revoked.description: Ids of keys whose signatures are refused even when valid, e.g. `"F7C5EF0A9B1D2E3C"`.

ToolTrust.description: Whether cuilo may run a project's tools, which run with the user's rights.

oneOf.description: Ask once per project in a terminal and remember the answer; elsewhere, only in trusted projects.

ToolsConfig.description: Project tools such as Biome or Prettier.

UpdatePolicy.description: What cuilo does about new releases; checks run in the background, never outside a terminal or in CI.

oneOf.description: Install them in the background, signature checked, when the install script installed cuilo; otherwise print a notice.
Print a notice, at most once a day, saying to run `cuilo upgrade`.
Never look for them; `cuilo upgrade` still works.

description: The user's own config, outside every project: `<config dir>/cuilo/config.toml`.

ast_grep.description: The ast-grep program for pack migrations, e.g. `["bunx", "@ast-grep/cli"]`; default `ast-grep`.

auth.description: Credentials for pack downloads by host, e.g. `github.com`; the token comes from an environment variable.

patchers.description: External tools that replace the built-in patchers, by patch kind.

signing.description: Trusted signing keys, and whether packs must be signed.

tools.description: When cuilo may run a project's own formatters and linters on the files it generates.

updates.description: What cuilo does about new releases, which it looks for at most once a day in a terminal: `auto`, `notify` or `off`; `CUILO_UPDATES` overrides it. Default `auto`.

wire.description:
Whether `cuilo add` applies pieces' wiring steps, such as mounting new routes in the app's entry
file, instead of listing them as next steps; `--wire` and `--no-wire` override it.

title: UserConfig
